title: The Georgia Vowels and the Two Temporary Tombs: Soong Mei-ling, the Republic's English Voice
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Shanghai, the disputed birth
stops.date_confidence: year attested; her passport gives 4 March 1898, but East Asian age reckoning has produced 5 March and the year 1897 in other sources, and the place is contested between Neishidi in Pudong (English Wikipedia) and Tongren Hospital inside the International Settlement (Chinese Wikipedia); the pin is the city, not a house
stops.campa: A daughter is born to Charlie Soong, Hainan-born, Methodist-trained, printer of Bibles and financier of revolutions, and to Ni Kwei-tseng. They name her Mei-ling. Her sisters Ai-ling and Ching-ling are already in the house; her brother T.V. Soong will grow up to hold the Republic's purse. The city she is born into is three cities at once, Chinese, French, and International, and the family belongs entirely to none of them. Even the room is disputed: a family house at Neishidi out in Pudong, or a hospital ward inside the Settlement.
suggested_refs: The Neishidi house at Chuansha, Pudong, and Tongren Hospital in the International Settlement, the two candidate birthplaces

stops.name: Wenchang, Hainan: the village the name came from
stops.date_confidence: undated in the sources; the ancestral tie is genealogical rather than lived, and is placed here at the year of her birth as a marker only
stops.campa: Two hundred miles south across the strait, in the Wen River country of Hainan, stands the house the Soongs came from. Charlie Soong left it as a boy, shipped to Boston and then to a Methodist college in North Carolina, and came back to Shanghai an American-made Chinese. None of his children ever live here. The tie is a name on a genealogy and a shrine that later governments will restore for visitors. Mei-ling's Hainan is inherited at second hand, in her father's accent and in his church.
suggested_refs: The Soong Ancestral Residence at Gulou, east of Wenchang city, Hainan
sources: Hainan local histories, cited at second hand; not verified against primary Soong-family records

stops.name: Summit, New Jersey: sent west at nine
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January
stops.campa: At nine she is put on a ship for America, the third of the Soong daughters sent out on the same theory: that the coming China will need women who can argue with foreigners in the foreigners' own language. She is enrolled at a private school in Summit, New Jersey, among girls who have never heard of the Yangtze. English becomes the language she thinks in. When she returns to Shanghai a decade later she will speak it better than she speaks Mandarin, and she will spend years correcting that.
suggested_refs: The private school at Summit, New Jersey, her first American schooling

stops.name: Demorest, Georgia: the eighth grade at Piedmont College
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January
stops.campa: She follows her sister Ching-ling south to Georgia, where Wesleyan College at Macon has already taken two Soongs and will not take a ten-year-old. She is parked instead in the eighth grade at Piedmont College in Demorest, in the Blue Ridge foothills, in a town of a few hundred people. The legend that she enrolled at Wesleyan at ten is a compression of this arrangement: attached to the campus, boarded near it, taught elsewhere until she was old enough to be admitted properly.
suggested_refs: Piedmont College at Demorest, Georgia, wrongly located in Tennessee by several summaries of her life

stops.name: Monteagle, Tennessee: Fairmount College
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January
stops.campa: Two years on she is moved again, to Fairmount College on the Cumberland Plateau at Monteagle, a summer-assembly town of Methodist camp meetings and chautauqua lecturers. The itinerary of these years is a chain of small denominational schools in the American South, each holding her a year or two until the next one takes her. She has no fixed house and no parent on the continent, and her surname defeats everyone who tries it. She is twelve and has been abroad three years. Three more will pass before she is a college student in her own name.
suggested_refs: Fairmount College at Monteagle, Tennessee, on the Cumberland Plateau

stops.name: Macon, Georgia: registered a freshman at Wesleyan
stops.date_confidence: year attested, age fifteen; month and day unknown, defaulted to January. The pin is the College Street campus she actually attended, not the Forsyth Road campus the college moved to in 1928
stops.campa: At fifteen she is finally registered as a freshman at Wesleyan College on College Street in Macon, in her own name and her own right. Ai-ling has graduated and gone home; Ching-ling is in her last years here. The three Soong sisters pass through the same Georgia college in sequence and come out of it holding the same instrument, an American education to be wielded in Chinese politics. Wesleyan will keep her in its records forever, and she will keep Georgia in her vowels for ninety-one years.
suggested_refs: The old College Street campus of Wesleyan College, Macon, Georgia, before the 1928 move

stops.name: Wellesley, Massachusetts: the transfer north
stops.date_confidence: year attested, two years after the Wesleyan registration; month and day unknown, defaulted to January. The incoming research pool dated this June 1913, which is a year early
stops.campa: After two years in Macon she transfers north to Wellesley, outside Boston, to be within reach of her brother T.V., then at Harvard. It is the first time since she was nine that a member of her family lives close enough to visit. She reads English literature and takes philosophy, and joins the Tau Zeta Epsilon society. The lake, the library, the New England winter: this is the landscape she will describe as her second home for the next eighty years, in a country that will alternately adore her and file reports on her.
suggested_refs: Wellesley College and the Tau Zeta Epsilon society house
sources: Wellesley College alumnae records, cited at second hand

stops.name: Wellesley, the Durant Scholar takes her degree
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: She takes her degree in English literature as a Durant Scholar, the college's highest academic distinction, on the nineteenth of June. She is nineteen years old and has spent half her life in America. Nothing in the Wellesley curriculum has prepared her for the use she will make of it. She will interpret at Cairo between Roosevelt and Churchill, and she will carry a Chinese state's case to the West for thirty years in the accent of a Georgia boarding school. She sails for Shanghai within weeks.
suggested_refs: Wellesley's Durant Scholar rolls for the class of 1917
sources: Wellesley College alumnae records, cited at second hand

stops.name: Shanghai, the ship home
stops.date_confidence: month approximate; she graduated 19 June 1917 and sailed within weeks, the arrival date itself unattested in the sources consulted
stops.campa: She lands at Shanghai after ten years away and finds she is a foreigner in her father's house. Her English is unaccented American; her Mandarin, by her own later account, is not equal to the room. She hires tutors and begins on the classics as an adult beginner, learning her own country the way her classmates at Wellesley learned French. Shanghai in 1917 is full of returned students doing exactly this. Very few of them will be required to make the acquired language carry a nation's argument.
suggested_refs: The returned-student milieu of treaty-port Shanghai after 1917
sources: Pakula, 'The Last Empress', cited at second hand and not read in this session

stops.name: Shanghai, the introduction to Chiang Kai-shek
stops.date_confidence: contested and left contested: English Wikipedia dates the meeting to 1920, while the most commonly repeated biographical account places it in Shanghai in 1922 at a gathering in Sun Yat-sen's residence. The earlier date is used. The pool's Guangzhou setting is supported by neither and is dropped
stops.campa: Through Ching-ling, who has married Sun Yat-sen, she enters the circle around the Nationalist leadership and meets a rising officer named Chiang Kai-shek. The accounts do not agree on the year, and the corpus does not adjudicate them. In November 1922 a ship carrying Albert Einstein touches this same port, and a telegram relayed through Shanghai tells him he has won the Nobel Prize. In these same years, in this same city, a woman educated in Georgia is introduced to the man who will govern China.
suggested_refs: Sun Yat-sen's Shanghai residence, given by tradition as the setting of the first meeting
sources: corpus interlock: canonical Republican-era Shanghai pin inherited byte-identical from mao_zedong.journey.json
corpus interlock: einstein.journey.json, Shanghai Nobel-telegram stop, November 1922

stops.name: Seymour Road, Shanghai: the private ceremony
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: At the Soong house at 369 Seymour Road a private religious ceremony is held before the public one. Chiang has had to satisfy the mother. He is already married, in the older Chinese way, and he is not a Christian. He agrees to study the Bible. He does not agree to be baptised, and tells Ni Kwei-tseng why. The marriage joins the Nationalist army to the Shanghai financial world, and hands the Generalissimo a wife who can talk to America in America's own language.
stops.quote: religion needed to be gradually absorbed, not swallowed like a pill
stops.quote_source: Chiang Kai-shek to Ni Kwei-tseng, on declining immediate baptism, as reported in Wikipedia, 'Soong Mei-ling'
suggested_refs: The Soong residence at 369 Seymour Road, now 369 Shaanxi North Road, Shanghai

stops.name: The Majestic Hotel, Shanghai: the public wedding
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: That afternoon more than a thousand guests fill the ballroom of the Majestic Hotel on Gordon Road, beneath an enormous portrait of Sun Yat-sen and the flags of the Republic. The photographers of three continents are present and the pictures run everywhere. From this day the two names are printed together. The Chinese state acquires, for the first time in its history, a first lady built for the foreign press with the deliberation of a warship, and the foreign press acquires the only Chinese figure it will ever feel it understands.
suggested_refs: The Majestic Hotel (Dahua Fandian), Gordon Road near Bubbling Well Road, Shanghai, demolished in the 1930s
sources: North-China Herald wedding coverage, December 1927, cited at second hand

stops.name: Shanghai, the Generalissimo is baptised
stops.date_confidence: year inferred: English Wikipedia dates the baptism three years after the December 1927 marriage; month and day unknown, defaulted to January
stops.campa: Three years after the wedding Chiang Kai-shek is baptised in the Soong family's Methodist church, having kept his word by taking his time. The Generalissimo of a Confucian republic becomes a Christian by marriage, and the Christianity in question arrives by way of a Hainan boy trained in North Carolina. It is the far end of a road opened by Matteo Ricci, who died in Beijing in 1610 and lies at Zhalan: three hundred and twenty years of mission work, terminating in a marriage contract signed on Seymour Road.
suggested_refs: The Soong family's Methodist church in Shanghai, where Chiang was baptised in 1930
sources: corpus interlock: matteo_ricci.journey.json, and mao_zedong.journey.json's note on Ricci's grave at Zhalan

stops.name: Nanjing, the Committee of Yuans
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January. The Legislative Yuan membership runs 1930 to 1932
stops.campa: With the capital moved from Peking to Nanjing, she is appointed to the Committee of Yuans, and from 1930 to 1932 she sits as a member of the Legislative Yuan. The Presidential Palace on Changjiang Road is the seat of the government and her husband's office, not their house; she goes there to work. She translates, drafts, receives, and answers the foreign correspondents her husband cannot. In October 1931 Time puts her on its cover. Three more covers will follow, and one of them will name her jointly with him.
suggested_refs: The Presidential Palace on Changjiang Road, Nanjing, seat of the Nationalist Government

stops.name: Nanchang, the New Life Movement
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested; day unknown, defaulted to the first
stops.campa: From Nanchang, headquarters of the campaign against the Communists in Jiangxi, the couple launch the New Life Movement: Confucian propriety, hygiene, punctuality, and the four virtues, preached to a peasantry the Nationalists are otherwise losing. She writes its English-language case and supplies its moral vocabulary. The movement issues rules about spitting, about buttons, about the correct way to eat in public, and it is meant as a weapon. The enemy it is aimed at is at that moment walking out of Jiangxi on the Long March.
suggested_refs: The New Life Movement founding documents, Nanchang, February 1934
sources: New Life Movement founding documents, cited at second hand

stops.name: Guling, Mount Lu: the villa named Meilu
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January
stops.campa: On Mount Lu above the Yangtze plain, in the missionary hill station of Guling, she is given a stone villa and it is named for her: Meilu, Mei's cottage. The Nanjing government summers here, out of the river heat, in a town built by Protestant missionaries for precisely this purpose. Officials climb the mountain steps to find the Generalissimo among rhododendrons. The habit of the cool mountain in August is one of the very few she will carry unbroken off the mainland and into the island years.
suggested_refs: Meilu Villa at Guling on Mount Lu, Jiangxi, preserved as a museum
sources: Lushan National Park heritage records, cited at second hand

stops.name: Nanjing, Meiling Palace below Purple Mountain
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: completed 1934, presented to her on her birthday, 4 March 1936; the couple moved in that summer
stops.campa: Below Purple Mountain, near the tomb of Sun Yat-sen, a villa of green glazed tile has been standing since 1934. Chiang gives it to her on her birthday: three storeys, a chapel, a garden, and an aerial plan that later visitors will say resembles a necklace with a pendant hung from it. They move in that summer. After 1946 it becomes his official residence, and long after both of them are gone it becomes a museum in a country neither of them governs, its basement hung with her own paintings.
suggested_refs: Meiling Palace, No. 9 Zhongshanling, Nanjing, now a house museum

stops.name: Nanjing, Secretary-General of the Aeronautical Affairs Commission
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January
stops.campa: She is made Secretary-General of the Chinese Aeronautical Affairs Commission, which is to say that the Republic's air force is handed to a Wellesley graduate in English literature. She buys aircraft, argues with contractors, and recruits the American airmen who will become the Flying Tigers. In April 1938 a magazine cover will style her Deputy Commander of the Republic of China Air Force, a title the record does not otherwise confirm. The pilots take to calling her their honorary commander, and she answers to it.
suggested_refs: The Chinese Aeronautical Affairs Commission and the recruitment of the American Volunteer Group

stops.name: Nanjing, the decision against the punitive expedition
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by her own narrative, which records reaching Nanking on Sunday morning, 13 December 1936
stops.campa: Word reaches her that her husband has been seized at the hot springs of Huaqing, near Xi'an, by his own generals. Zhang Xueliang sends assurances that he is alive. She reaches Nanjing on the Sunday morning and finds the government there resolving on a punitive expedition of bombers and armies, which she is certain will get Chiang killed inside a week. Against the generals she argues for negotiation instead. She holds no office that entitles her to argue at all, and she argues them down.
stops.quote: So, rightly or wrongly, I decided to fight it and strive for a quick, calm and bloodless settlement of the whole affair.
stops.quote_source: Mayling Soong Chiang, 'Sian: A Coup d'Etat,' in General Chiang Kai-shek: The Account of the Fortnight in Sian (Doubleday, Doran, 1937), printed p.67; written of Nanking, 13-14 December 1936
suggested_refs: Her own narrative 'Sian: A Coup d'Etat', published 1937
sources: General Chiang Kai-shek: The Account of the Fortnight in Sian (1937), archive.org generalchiangkai00chia, full text checked

stops.name: Xi'an, the flight to the captors
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: She flies into Xi'an with her brother T.V. Soong and with Dai Li, chief of the secret police, into a city held by the men holding her husband. Nanjing's generals had told her it was suicide. Chiang, under guard and refusing on principle to negotiate with his own subordinates, is astonished to see her walk in. From the twenty-second the talks are hers as much as anyone's. She is the wife of the hostage and the sister-in-law of the Republic's founder, and she is the only person in the building whom every faction has a reason not to shoot.
suggested_refs: The Huaqing Pool at Lintong, where Chiang was seized on 12 December 1936; no source places her there

stops.name: Xi'an, the table with Zhou Enlai
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: On Christmas Eve she sits at a table with Zhou Enlai, Zhang Xueliang, and Yang Hucheng. What is agreed there ends, in principle, the civil war: the Communist Party is to be legalised, the armies are to face Japan instead of each other, the united front is to exist. Zhou has come down from the north to save the life of the man who has spent ten years hunting him. The agreements are never signed and never published. They hold anyway, more or less, for the eight years of the Japanese war.
suggested_refs: The unsigned Xi'an agreements of 24 December 1936 and the Second United Front

stops.name: Xi'an, the release
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the party took off around 5 pm on 25 December and reached Nanjing on 26 December, correcting the widespread claim that they arrived the same day
stops.campa: She asks Zhang Xueliang for her husband and he gives him up. At five in the afternoon on Christmas Day the plane lifts out of Xi'an carrying Chiang, his wife, and his captor, who is flying to Nanjing voluntarily to submit to punishment and will spend the next half century under arrest for it. They land the following day. Chiang comes home a national figure of a kind he was not a fortnight earlier, and she comes home as the woman who went in and got him out.
suggested_refs: Zhang Xueliang's voluntary return to Nanjing and his fifty-four years of detention

stops.name: Hankou, the government moves upriver
stops.date_confidence: month approximate; the relocation follows the fall of Nanjing in December 1937 and the Hankou period runs into 1938
stops.campa: Nanjing falls in December and the killing inside it runs for six weeks. The government has already gone upriver to Hankou, and she works there on refugee relief, on the war-orphan schools she is beginning to organise, and on the air force she is still nominally in charge of. She has been broadcasting to America since the summer, in the English she learned in Georgia, and the American public is starting to hear the war in China in a voice it recognises as very nearly its own.
suggested_refs: The Nationalist government's Hankou period, December 1937 to October 1938
sources: Wartime Nationalist government records, cited at second hand

stops.name: Chongqing, the bombed capital
stops.date_confidence: the Chongqing years run 1938 to 1945; the entry date is approximate and defaulted to January. The pin is the canonical corpus Chongqing coordinate, not the Huangshan compound in Nan'an District where the couple actually lived
stops.campa: The government goes further up the Yangtze to Chongqing, into the fog and the bombing. The Chiangs base themselves at a hillside compound at Huangshan on the south bank. For seven years she runs war-orphan programmes and air force welfare from a capital that is attacked from the air more or less continuously, and receives the American journalists and generals on whom the Republic's supply line depends. Chongqing is where her reputation is made, and where, among the Americans, it begins to come apart.
stops.quote: Chinese socialism, if you like to call it that, seeks above all else to preserve the birthrights of the individual.
stops.quote_source: Madame Chiang Kai-shek, 'China Emergent,' The Atlantic, May 1942 (article fetched and read in full; the hedging clause is routinely deleted when the line is quoted)
suggested_refs: The Huangshan wartime residence in Nan'an District, Chongqing, across the Yangtze from the city
sources: corpus interlock: canonical Chongqing pin inherited byte-identical from mao_zedong.journey.json

stops.name: Kunming, the dinner for the Flying Tigers
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the printed heading of the speech
stops.campa: At a dinner she and her husband give in Kunming for the American Volunteer Group, she stands to speak to a room of contracted pilots who have been fighting for China since December. She is their honorary commander and she calls them her boys. Claire Chennault answers her. Within four months the group will be absorbed into the United States Army Air Forces; for now it is a private air force flying for a country not its own, bought by a woman with a degree in English literature, and she is the one who stands up to thank it.
stops.quote: You have flown across the Pacific in China's gravest hour on wings of hope and faith.
stops.quote_source: Speech to the American Volunteer Group, Kunming, 28 February 1942; The Voice of China (Hutchinson, 1944), printed p.16
suggested_refs: The Voice of China (Hutchinson, 1944), 'Salute to the Flying Tigers', pp.16-19
sources: The Voice of China (Hutchinson, 1944), archive.org voiceofchinaspee00chia, full text checked

stops.name: The White House, Washington: a guest of the Roosevelts
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested; day unknown, defaulted to the first
stops.campa: She arrives in Washington as the guest of Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt and stays in the house, where she rings for servants at night and speaks to the staff the way a Soong speaks to staff. Asked at dinner how the Generalissimo would deal with a coalminers' strike, she draws a fingernail slowly across her throat. The First Lady says nothing at the table. The remark she makes afterwards, in private, will follow this visit into every account of it written since.
stops.quote: She can talk beautifully about democracy, but does not know how to live democracy.
stops.quote_source: Eleanor Roosevelt, private remark, 1943, reported in Sterling Seagrave, The Soong Dynasty (1985) and quoted in the Guardian obituary of Madame Chiang Kai-shek, 25 October 2003. Second-hand throughout: not attested in Roosevelt's own published writing
suggested_refs: Eleanor Roosevelt's memoirs and the White House visitor records for February 1943
sources: AP-derived obituaries, Chicago Tribune and Sydney Morning Herald, 25 October 2003

stops.name: Washington, the address to the House of Representatives
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The pin is the canonical corpus Washington coordinate, not the Capitol building itself
stops.campa: She stands before the House of Representatives, the first Chinese national and the second woman to address the Congress of the United States, and speaks without an interpreter in the English of a Georgia boarding school. The chamber rises to her. Five and a half years of war, the Burma Road, the bombing of Chongqing, and the Republic's need for materiel are delivered to America in America's own cadence, by a woman America has already decided it knows. Enrico Fermi carried a different warning into this city in 1939.
stops.quote: We in China, like you, want a better world not for ourselves alone but for all mankind, and we must have it.
stops.quote_source: 'A Better World for All Mankind', address to the United States House of Representatives, 18 February 1943; The Voice of China (Hutchinson, 1944), printed p.87
suggested_refs: The Voice of China, 'A Better World for All Mankind', pp.87-88, closing: 'Man's mettle is tested both in adversity and success. Doubly is this true of the soul of a nation.'
sources: The Voice of China (Hutchinson, 1944), archive.org voiceofchinaspee00chia, full text checked
corpus interlock: canonical Washington pin inherited byte-identical from fermi.journey.json

stops.name: The Waldorf Astoria, New York: the fundraising base
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested; day unknown, defaulted to the first
stops.campa: She takes rooms at the Waldorf Astoria and works New York from them: society donors, publishers, the China lobby, and Henry Luce of Time, who has already given her three covers and who was himself born in China to Presbyterian missionaries. United China Relief raises money in a country fourteen months into its own war and six years into reading about hers. The hotel is accustomed to galas. It has not previously housed a foreign government's entire case for its own survival.
suggested_refs: United China Relief and the Henry Luce publications' promotion of the Chiangs
sources: Contemporary New York press coverage, February 1943, cited at second hand

stops.name: Madison Square Garden, New York: the rally
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The pin is the third Madison Square Garden, on Eighth Avenue between 49th and 50th Streets, demolished in 1968; the name now points to a building a mile and a half south that did not then exist
stops.campa: She fills the Garden on Eighth Avenue for a rally on China's behalf, one of the largest crowds of the tour and of her life. She does not ask for pity. She asks for materiel, and she asks the United States to notice that the war it entered fifteen months ago has been fought by China since 1937. The building she speaks in will be pulled down within a generation, and the pin that carries its name will migrate a mile and a half south to a hall she never entered.
suggested_refs: The third Madison Square Garden, Eighth Avenue at 49th to 50th Streets, demolished 1968
sources: New York Times coverage, March 1943, cited at second hand

stops.name: The Hollywood Bowl, Los Angeles: thirty thousand
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Crowds reported as large as thirty thousand come to the Hollywood Bowl to hear her. The studios turn out; the tour has by now taken in Washington, New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Los Angeles, and this is the largest single audience of her life. She is forty-five, photographed in a black cheongsam under the Hollywood hills, and for one spring she is the most admired foreign woman in the United States. Within two years American officers back from Chongqing will be filing reports that dismantle most of what this spring built.
suggested_refs: Los Angeles Times coverage of the Hollywood Bowl address, April 1943
sources: Los Angeles Times coverage, April 1943, cited at second hand

stops.name: Parliament Hill, Ottawa: the case made twice
stops.date_confidence: month and year reported but not independently confirmed here; day unknown, defaulted to the first. The Canadian parliamentary record was not fetched in this research and the stop is carried as reconstruction
stops.campa: She carries the tour north to the Canadian House of Commons and makes the same case to a smaller parliament in a country three and a half years into the war. The Canadian record of the visit is thinner than the American coverage, and the detail of this leg is reconstructed rather than documented here. In the spring and summer of 1943 the appeal for China goes out in two capitals of the English-speaking world, not one, and in the same borrowed accent.
suggested_refs: The Canadian House of Commons record for June 1943
sources: Canadian parliamentary record, 1943, cited at second hand and not fetched

stops.name: Cairo, the conference near the pyramids
stops.date_confidence: the conference ran 22 to 26 November 1943; the date given is the second day. The pin is the canonical corpus Cairo coordinate, not the ambassador's villa at Giza where the sessions were actually held
stops.campa: At the conference outside Cairo she sits between Roosevelt, Churchill, and her husband, and she interprets. The sessions are not at the Mena House, which merely houses the delegations, but at the American ambassador's residence near the Giza pyramids. Everything China says at Cairo passes through her mouth into English and everything said to China passes back through it. Gustave Flaubert came up this same river in 1850 to look at ruins. She comes to the same city to set a border settlement for postwar Asia.
suggested_refs: The residence of Ambassador Alexander Comstock Kirk near the Giza pyramid complex, site of the Cairo Conference sessions
sources: corpus interlock: canonical Cairo pin inherited byte-identical from gustave_flaubert.journey.json

stops.name: Chongqing, Mao Zedong flies in
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Mao Zedong flies into Chongqing on the twenty-eighth of August and stays forty-three days, negotiating face to face with Chiang Kai-shek for the first time in eighteen years. Patrick Hurley has guaranteed his safety in person. Photographs are taken of the two men raising glasses to each other. She is resident in the wartime capital through the whole of it, the Republic's English voice at every reception, and the agreement the two sides sign in October will last until the following summer.
suggested_refs: The Double Tenth Agreement of 10 October 1945, signed at Chongqing
sources: corpus interlock: mao_zedong.journey.json, stop 'Chongqing, forty-three days with Chiang'

stops.name: Nanjing, the government returns
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January
stops.campa: The government returns to Nanjing after eight years, and Meiling Palace becomes the Generalissimo's official residence. She resumes the old role: translator, hostess, the face turned toward Washington. The civil war that the Xi'an agreements suspended has resumed and is going badly. American mediation under Marshall collapses inside a year. The villa Chiang gave her for her birthday in 1936 is now the household of a government losing a country, and they will keep it for three years.
suggested_refs: Meiling Palace as Chiang's official residence, 1946 to 1949
sources: Republic of China government records, 1946-1949, cited at second hand

stops.name: Washington, the last appeal
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: she left China on 28 November 1948, met Marshall on 3 December and Truman on 10 December. The pin is the canonical corpus Washington coordinate
stops.campa: She leaves for the United States on the twenty-eighth of November with the Republic collapsing behind her, and goes to Washington to ask for money. She sees Marshall on the third of December and Truman on the tenth. She gets nothing. The Congress that rose for her in 1943 has read five years of dispatches about her husband's government since. Washington has learned, in the decade since Enrico Fermi's warning was carried into it, to settle the fate of distant countries in single afternoons, and it settles hers.
suggested_refs: Her meetings with Secretary Marshall, 3 December 1948, and President Truman, 10 December 1948
sources: corpus interlock: canonical Washington pin inherited byte-identical from fermi.journey.json

stops.name: New York, the year of waiting
stops.date_confidence: she was in the United States continuously from 28 November 1948 to 13 January 1950; the date given is the day of Mao's departure for Moscow, used to fix the stop. The pin is the canonical corpus New York coordinate
stops.campa: She does not go back. Through 1949 she stays in America while the mainland is lost province by province, a first lady of a government with almost no territory left. On the sixteenth of December Mao Zedong boards a train for Moscow, nine days to the Kremlin, his first journey outside China, and Stalin receives him. She is in New York, in the city where Buckminster Fuller is drawing his domes, waiting to learn whether there will be a country left to be first lady of.
suggested_refs: Her fourteen months in the United States, November 1948 to January 1950

segments.name: Taiwan, and the Long Coda in New York

stops.name: Songshan Airport, Taipei: the late arrival
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. She was not present for the December 1949 evacuation, contrary to the widespread claim that she followed her husband to Taiwan in 1949
stops.campa: She flies into Songshan on the thirteenth of January, fourteen months after she left the mainland and a full year after the evacuation she is usually said to have shared. The Nationalist government has been on Taiwan since December 1949 and has managed without her. She arrives to a rump republic on an island of thirteen thousand square miles, still carrying the name and the seat of a country the size of Europe, and she will live here, on and off, for the next thirty-eight years.
suggested_refs: Songshan Airport, Taipei, and the Nationalist relocation of December 1949

stops.name: The Shilin Official Residence, Taipei
stops.date_confidence: the Shilin years run from 1950 to 1975; the entry month is approximate, following her arrival on 13 January 1950
stops.campa: The Shilin residence in the north of Taipei becomes their house for a quarter of a century: a Chinese garden, a Western garden, a rose garden of her own, and a small chapel Chiang calls the Victory Chapel because it is where he prays for the return. She paints, in the classical manner, having taken it up in middle age. What else she does across these twenty-five years is thinly recorded outside Taiwan. It is the least documented stretch of an extremely public life, and the atlas leaves the gap open.
suggested_refs: The Shilin Official Residence Park, Taipei, and Chiang's Victory Chapel
sources: Shilin Residence Park heritage records, Taipei

stops.name: Cihu, Daxi: the temporary tomb
stops.date_confidence: Chiang died 5 April 1975; the interment date is approximate and defaulted to the start of the month
stops.campa: Chiang Kai-shek dies in April and is not buried. He is laid in a black marble sarcophagus at Cihu in Daxi, in a lakeside house built because the country around it resembles Fenghua, where he was born and where he means to lie once the mainland is recovered. The arrangement is described as temporary and stays that way. Her own crypt will be described the same way. In February 2018 activists break into the chamber, and afterwards the coffin is viewed only through glass.
suggested_refs: Cihu Mausoleum, Daxi District, Taoyuan, and the 28 February 2018 vandalism of the sarcophagus chamber

stops.name: Lattingtown, Long Island: thirty-six acres
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the departure follows Chiang's death in April 1975 and a breast cancer diagnosis, and the month is approximate
stops.campa: Diagnosed with breast cancer, and with her stepson Chiang Ching-kuo now running Taipei, she leaves for New York and does not come back for thirteen years. The estate at Lattingtown on the North Shore of Long Island runs to thirty-six acres. She is seventy-seven. The widow of the Generalissimo settles into a Gold Coast house among Soong relatives, receives Republican senators, paints, and proceeds to outlive the entire generation that made and lost the Republic of China on the mainland.
suggested_refs: The thirty-six-acre Lattingtown estate, her principal United States residence from 1975 to 2000

stops.name: Taipei, the return after Chiang Ching-kuo
stops.date_confidence: year attested; Chiang Ching-kuo died 13 January 1988 and her return follows, the exact date not established in the sources consulted
stops.campa: Chiang Ching-kuo dies in January and she flies back to Taipei, where a party she has outlasted is choosing a Taiwanese-born successor. She is ninety. She has a view about the succession and it does not prevail. Lee Teng-hui takes the presidency and the island begins turning into a country different from the one her husband ruled. She stays some years and then returns to New York for good. Taiwan's last sight of her falls in the middle of the nineteen-nineties.
suggested_refs: The Kuomintang succession of January 1988 and the accession of Lee Teng-hui

stops.name: Washington, the Capitol reception at ninety-seven
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested; day unknown, defaulted to the first. The pin is the canonical corpus Washington coordinate
stops.campa: At ninety-seven she comes to Capitol Hill for a reception marking the fiftieth anniversary of the end of the war. Members of Congress stand for her again in the building where she spoke in 1943, and hardly one of them held a seat on the first occasion. She makes her last visit to Taiwan in the same period. She is the last surviving principal of the alliance, older than the People's Republic, older than the United Nations, older than the war she came to this city to ask help for.
stops.quote: I came to school in the United States, and I will always consider America my second home.
stops.quote_source: Widely attributed to her 1995 remarks marking the fiftieth anniversary of the end of the war; carried on Wikiquote without a traceable primary citation and not verified against any fetched document
suggested_refs: The Capitol Hill reception of July 1995, fifty years after the end of the war
sources: Congressional Record and press coverage, July 1995

stops.name: 10 Gracie Square, Manhattan: the last address
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown, defaulted to January. The incoming research pool dated this residence from 1975, which is twenty-five years early
stops.campa: She sells the Lattingtown estate and moves into an apartment at 10 Gracie Square, a cooperative building on the East River at the end of Eighty-fourth Street. She is a hundred and two years old. The apartment is quiet, well guarded, and hung with her own paintings. Reporters who apply for interviews are told she is unavailable. She has been a public figure for seventy-three years, since a ballroom on Gordon Road in Shanghai, and she has decided she is finished being one.
suggested_refs: 10 Gracie Square, Manhattan, a cooperative apartment building on the East River
sources: New York property and obituary records, cited at second hand

stops.name: Manhattan, death at one hundred and five
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. She died in her sleep in her own apartment; the claim found in some summaries that the location of death is disputed, or that she died in hospital, is supported by no source consulted
stops.campa: She dies in her sleep in her apartment on the twenty-third of October, one hundred and five years old. She was born a subject of the Qing dynasty and dies in the third year of the twenty-first century. She has outlived her husband by twenty-eight years, the mainland Republic she represented by fifty-four, and every American president she ever lobbied. The government in Taipei sends condolences to New York, to an address in a country that was her second home for ninety-six of her years.
suggested_refs: The New York Times obituary of 24 October 2003

stops.name: Ferncliff Cemetery, Hartsdale: the second temporary tomb
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested; day unknown, defaulted to the first
stops.campa: She is placed in a crypt at Ferncliff in Hartsdale, in Westchester County, among Soong family members. Wikipedia's account of the cemetery does not say which of the three mausoleums holds her. The interment is called temporary. The stated intention is that she and Chiang be buried together on the mainland once the differences across the strait are resolved. He is still at Cihu behind glass; she is still at Ferncliff. Two temporary tombs, one on each side of the Pacific, waiting on a condition that has not been met.
suggested_refs: Ferncliff Cemetery, Hartsdale, New York, and the unfulfilled intention of a joint mainland burial
